newsitem.title: TURKEY: Islamist MP says Turk-Israel exercise unnecessary.
newsitem.headline: Islamist MP says Turk-Israel exercise unnecessary.

text.p: A close aide to Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Friday he saw no need for joint naval exercises with Israel in a sign of Islamist disquiet over growing relations with the Jewish state.

"This is not a subject which has been discussed by the government...I say there is no need for such a thing," Oguzhan Asilturk, an MP and a deputy chairman of Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party, told a news conference.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, expressed opposition to closer cooperation with Israel before coming to power last June.
However, Turkey's powerful military, spearheading an anti-Islamist campaign by the secularist establishment, has overridden his objections.

Turkish Deputy Chief of Staff General Cevik Bir held talks with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai earlier this week to discuss joint naval exercises with Israel and the United States in the eastern Mediterranean.

Iran and much of the Arab world have expressed unease at Turkey's growing defence ties with the Jewish state. A deal signed last year has allowed Israeli air force jets to train in the ample airspace of Turkey, a Moslem but secular country.
Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf, in remarks published on Friday, sharply criticised the plans for naval exercises.
"Iraq strongly denounces these manoeuvres and considers them a provocative and hostile act against the Arab nation," Sahaf said in a statement carried by Iraqi newspapers.
"The participation of a state (Turkey) whose people are Moslems with the Zionist entity...is not an ordinary act," Sahaf said, in a reference to Israel.
Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said in a statement published on Thursday that Lebanon was deeply concerned with the U.S.-Turkish-Israeli alliance.
The Turkish Foreign Ministry has said the naval exercises, set to take place some time in the summer, do not pose a threat to neighbouring countries.
It said the manoeuvres would not have any strategic purpose and would be focused on search and rescue operations.
